title: Localization commutes with embedded-prime removal
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $M$ a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $M\to M'$ be the quotient supplied by [lem-sc-hilbert-embedded-points-affine-removal], and, for $f\in R$, let $M_f\to (M_f)'$ be the corresponding quotient for the localized module. Then $(M')_f\cong(M_f)'$.

proof.text: For any localization map g:M→N over R→A=S⁻¹R, prove Supp_A(N)=comap⁻¹(Supp_R(M)) directly from the element-annihilator characterization of support and the fraction equations. For S=powers(f), the induced map Supp(M_f)→Supp(M) is an open embedding, by PrimeSpectrum.localization_away_isOpenEmbedding and restriction to the inverse image of support. Preimages along an open embedding preserve nowhere density, so localization preserves nowhere-dense support.

proof.text: The support of a sum of submodules lies in the union of their supports: if both submodules vanish at a prime, multiply the two annihilators of a decomposition m=x+y to kill m outside that prime. A finite union of nowhere dense sets is nowhere dense. Therefore a maximal submodule with nowhere dense support contains every submodule with that property, by applying maximality to their sum.

proof.text: Let t be multiplication by f on the Noetherian module M. Apply LinearMap.eventually_iSup_ker_pow_eq and Module.End.eventually_disjoint_ker_pow_range_pow at a common n. An element killed by localization is killed by some f^k and hence belongs to ker(t^n). Its intersection with range(t^n) is zero. Thus localization is injective on f^n M.

proof.text: For N⊆M_f, let D be its inverse image in M and L=f^n D using Step 3. The Galois insertion Submodule.localized'gi gives D_f=N. The fraction identity (f^n m)/(f^n s)=m/s gives L_f=D_f=N. Localization is injective on L because L⊆f^n M. For any finite module whose localization map is injective, contraction of the annihilator of its localization equals its annihilator. By Module.support_eq_zeroLocus and PrimeSpectrum.closure_image_comap_zeroLocus, Supp(L) is the closure of the image of Supp(L_f). The same holds in Supp(M), by its induced topology. An inducing map sends a nowhere dense set to a nowhere dense set (Topology.IsInducing.isNowhereDense_image), and closure preserves nowhere density. Consequently, if N has nowhere dense support in Supp(M_f), L has nowhere dense support in Supp(M).
